source.quote: Table 33 'Input Data Types Supported by Tensor Core Acceleration per Compute Capability': row for CC 10.0 marks Yes for TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8; FP64 and INT4 cells blank (unsupported). FP32/FP64 are CUDA-Core precisions (not Tensor Core), so fp32 is carried in by the Blackwell 'Supported CUDA Core precisions' list.

Table 33 'Input Data Types Supported by Tensor Core Acceleration per Compute Capability': row for CC 10.3 marks Yes for TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8; FP6 and FP4 present but do NOT map to any v1 enum value; FP32 (CUDA-core) carried in by the Blackwell 'Supported CUDA Core precisions' list; INT4 cell blank (unsupported).

Table 33 'Input Data Types Supported by Tensor Core Acceleration per Compute Capability': the 12.x row (which includes 12.0) marks Yes for TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8; FP6 and FP4 present but do NOT map to any v1 enum value; FP32 (CUDA-core) carried in by the Blackwell 'Supported CUDA Core precisions' list; INT4 cell blank (unsupported).

fp4_fp6_note: NVIDIA Blackwell Architecture Technical Brief: 'new fifth-generation Tensor Core architecture in Blackwell supports new number formats such as FP4, including community-defined microscaling (OCP) formats. The Blackwell architecture supports all the data types and numerical formats listed in Table 1.' Table 1 (Blackwell Supported Data Types): FP64, FP32, TF32, FP16, BF16, FP8, INT8, FP6, FP4 — all confirmed present on Blackwell. NVIDIA Tensor Cores page: 'Supported Tensor Core precisions | FP64, TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, INT8, FP6, FP4' for Blackwell; NVFP4 blog: 'NVIDIA Blackwell provides maximum flexibility with support for FP64, FP32/TF32, FP16/BF16, INT8/FP8, FP6, and FP4 data formats.' Mapping onto the v1 precision enum [fp32,tf32,bf16,fp16,fp8,int8,int4]: (a) FP6 (6-bit floating point) is a native Blackwell Tensor Core format but has no analog in the v1 enum — it is not representable as tf32/bf16/fp16 and is ABSENT from the v1 enum; do NOT conflate with fp16. (b) FP4 (E2M1 4-bit floating point, incl. MXFP4/NVFP4 microscaling variants) is also a native Blackwell format; it does NOT map to the v1 int4 slot because int4 is signed INTEGER quantization whereas NVFP4/FP4 are floating 4-bit — so FP4 is likewise ABSENT from the v1 enum, and int4 is correctly absent for all Blackwell compute capabilities. Note: NVIDIA's own CUDA Table 33 lists FP6 and FP4 as Tensor Core input types for CC 10.x/12.x but lists INT4 as NOT supported (empty), so int4 must be omitted from every Blackwell card's precisions list; the float-precision FP4/FP6 are not captured by any v1 enum value. A standalone 'FP6' column is never enumerated in Table 33 — it always appears co-listed with FP8 ('FP8/FP6'), consistent with Blackwell's 'Total FP8/FP6 Tensor Core' spec-sheet line.
v1_enum_note: Each CC array is the v1-enum precision set per the repo's 4090/L40S convention (uniform across the family). The quoted Table 33 row gives the TENSOR-CORE input types; fp32 is CUDA-core; int4 is ABSENT for all Blackwell compute capabilities (Table 33 marks the INT4 cell blank for CC 10.0/10.3/12.0), and Blackwell-native FP6/FP4 are absent from the v1 enum (see fp4_fp6_note).
